sentences.text: 2  This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passe  ORDER Heard on the admission.
Admit.
With the consent of parties, heard finally.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 29/02/2012 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Anuppur (M.P.) in MACC No.28/2010, by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.1,96,000/- (One lakh ninety six thousand) with 6% interest to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries, which he has sustained in a motor vehicle accident.
2. According to claimant i.e. appellant herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, need to be enhanced.

3. Since, this appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out and if so to what extent?
4. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellant/claimant by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in the favour of claimant are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of filing an appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in a motor accident which took place on 09/10/2009 the appellant sustained multiple injuries in body including fracture of tibia and fibula bone in his right leg and his right leg was also badly ruptured and learned Tribunal has awarded a Vipin Kumar Gupta (Halwai) vs United India Insurance Company Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181510152/
2 sum of Rs.1,96,000/- (One lakh ninety six thousand) breakup of which is as under :
Rs.18,000/- Towards loss of income for six months Rs.50,000/- Towards pain and suffering Rs.8,000/- Towards transportation Rs.5,000/- Towards attendant Rs.5,000/- Towards future medical expenses Rs.1,10,000/- Towards expenses incurred in treatment 6.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that as per disability certificate (Ex.P/215)
appellant sustained 60% permanent disability, but the learned Claims Tribunal wrongly disbelieved the disability certificate (Ex.P/215) which was issued by medical board.
Learned counsel further submitted that in the accident appellant sustained fracture of tibia and fibula in his right leg and his right leg was also badly ruptured.
But the learned tribunal has not considered the future prospect of the appellant.
Learned tribunal has also disbelieved some medical bills, which were duly proved by the appellant, so that amount be also awarded in favour of appellant.

Learned counsel further submitted that meager amount has been awarded under the heads of transportation, special diet,
future treatment and pain and suffering.
It is prayed that the appeal be allowed and amount of compensation be enhanced substantially.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1 opposed the prayer and submitted in the incident appellant/injured sustained fracture of tibia and fibula bone in his right leg, which has recovered,
therefore, learned tribunal has rightly disbelieved the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P/215).
On other heads also amount awarded by the learned tribunal is just and proper hence, it is prayed that the appeal be dismissed.
8. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. From perusal of record it appears that in the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P-215) itself nature of disability is mentioned as "temporary", so the learned tribunal has rightly not awarded any amount towards permanent disability.

However, it appears that in the alleged incident appellant sustained fracture of tibia and fibula bone in his right leg, but the learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of grievous injury caused to the appellant in the alleged incident.
Similarly, no amount has been awarded towards special diet, which should be awarded.

In my considered opinion a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty thousand) will be sufficient to award under the head of grievous injury and Rs.5,000/- (Five thousand) will be just and proper to award towards special diet.
On other heads, amount awarded by the learned Tribunal appears to be just and proper.

10. In view of above discussion, appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation :-
Rs.18,000/- Towards loss of income for six months Rs.50,000/- Towards pain and suffering Rs.8,000/- Towards transportation Rs.5,000/- Towards future medical expenses Rs.5,000/- Towards attendant Rs.1,10,000/- Towards expenses incurred in treatment Rs.5,000/- Towards special diet.

3 Rs.50,000/-

sentences.text: Thus, appeal filed by the appellant/claimant is allowed.
The appellant/claimant will be entitled for a total sum of Rs.2,51,000/- (Two lakhs fifty one thousand) instead of Rs.1,96,000/- (One lakh ninety six thousand).
Thus, there shall be enhancement to the tune of Rs.55,000/- (Fifty five thousand), which shall fetch interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and condition of the award shall remain intact.

12. With the aforesaid, appeal stands disposed of.
13.
Records of the claims Tribunal be sent back alongwith the copy of this order for information and necessary compliance.
No order as to costs.
